recommendedWhen: Meeting room, classroom and BYOD/BYOM presentation workflows

salesLanguage.headline: MX-0402-MST-V2: makes the room easier for presenters to use
salesLanguage.plainEnglishSummary: Use this when people need to walk into a room, connect a laptop or room source, and get content onto the display without cable swapping or technical confusion.
salesLanguage.customerValue: It improves the day-to-day room experience by bringing source switching, display connection and often USB collaboration into one predictable room core.
salesLanguage.realWorldApplication: Meeting rooms, classrooms, training spaces and collaboration rooms where users need simple presentation from modern laptops.
salesLanguage.salespersonCue: Talk about the user journey: connect, present, share, hand off to the display or wider system.
talkTrack: It can support the USB side of collaboration, so cameras, speakerphones or USB devices can be part of the room workflow.
It is strongest when the customer wants a reliable wired room experience.
Use it where the display path stays local or is handled by another transport product.
discoveryPrompts: How many laptops or room sources need to connect?
Do users need USB devices such as a camera, speakerphone or touch display?
Are there one, two or more displays in the room?
Does the room need a feed for recording, Teams, Zoom, or AV-over-IP?
positioningNotes: Lead with user simplicity and room workflow.
Use the port count and USB class as proof after the application is understood.
avoidPositioningAs: Do not sell it as a generic matrix unless the customer only cares about source-to-display routing.
marketApplications: Meeting room, classroom and BYOD/BYOM presentation workflows

systemIntegrator.label: SI / installer
systemIntegrator.headline: MX-0402-MST-V2: deployment and commissioning view
systemIntegrator.pitch: Use this view when the installer needs to understand where the room core sits, which user connections land at the table or wall, and what leaves the room toward displays, USB devices or downstream systems.
systemIntegrator.value: Turns the sales conversation into practical install checks: location, cabling, signal direction, dependencies, control and commissioning risk.
talkTrack: Check the practical signal path around HDMI, USB-C, USB-C video input, USB 3.x before finalising the design.
Confirm what connects locally, what leaves the room, and which accessories or endpoints are required.
Check USB class, power method, control path and firmware notes before treating the product as a like-for-like substitute.
discoveryPrompts: Where will the product physically live: table, wall, display, rack, lectern or network closet?
What cable type, distance and route are available between each endpoint?
Which products, receivers, USB devices, controllers or network switches must be present for this to work?
How many laptops or room sources need to connect?
Do users need USB devices such as a camera, speakerphone or touch display?
positioningNotes: Good installer language should make dependencies visible before a quote is issued.
Call out install risk early when the product depends on USB bandwidth, network design, endpoint pairing or control integration.
Lead with user simplicity and room workflow.
Use the port count and USB class as proof after the application is understood.
avoidPositioningAs: Do not imply it is plug-and-play where cable distance, USB class, endpoint compatibility, network design or control programming still needs validation.
Do not sell it as a generic matrix unless the customer only cares about source-to-display routing.

consultant.label: Consultant / technical
consultant.headline: MX-0402-MST-V2: architecture fit and trade-off view
consultant.pitch: Use this view to decide whether the product is the right room-core architecture or whether the room should move toward a simpler switcher, matrix, extender or AV-over-IP design.
consultant.value: Helps separate a technically possible product choice from the strongest design choice for the application, budget, risk and future expansion.
talkTrack: Validate the application first, then decide whether this product family is the cleanest architecture.
Compare against simpler or more scalable alternatives where the requirement is fixed, expandable, distance-led or conferencing-led.
Use the specification as evidence after the room workflow and signal architecture are clear.
discoveryPrompts: Is this requirement driven by user experience, source/display routing, distance, USB, collaboration, network distribution, processing or control?
What would make this product the wrong choice even if it technically works?
Is the system expected to grow, change rooms, add endpoints, record, stream or integrate with a wider AV platform?
How many laptops or room sources need to connect?
Do users need USB devices such as a camera, speakerphone or touch display?
positioningNotes: Use for architectural judgement, product-family selection and proposal-safe trade-off language.
Be explicit when the product is technically possible but unlikely to be the most natural choice.
Lead with user simplicity and room workflow.
Use the port count and USB class as proof after the application is understood.
avoidPositioningAs: Do not let a feature match override the real application, architecture or operational requirement.
Do not sell it as a generic matrix unless the customer only cares about source-to-display routing.

technicalLines: 1x Analog Audio Out (5-pin Phoenix Male Connector)
USB-C IN/HDMI IN/ HDMI OUT: Up to 7.1ch, including PCM 2.0/5.1/7.1ch, Dolby Digital, Dolby Digital Plus, Dolby TrueHD, Dolby Atmos,
DTS 5.1, DTS-HD Master Audio and DTS:X.
All HDR formats, including HDR 10, HLG, HDR 10+ and Dolby Vision
Approx. 150W (Including USB Peripheral and USB-C charging)
Supports up to 4K@60Hz 4:4:4 video resolution on all HDMI inputs and outputs, ensuring superior visual quality for your presentations.
Supports a wide range of audio formats, including PCM 2.0/5.1/7.1ch, Dolby Digital, Dolby TrueHD, Dolby Atmos, DTS-HD Master Audio, and DTS, delivering an immersive audio experience.
Offers multiple control methods, including RS-232, Telnet, and a user-friendly Web UI, allowing for convenient management and configuration of the switcher.
Features automatic switching modes such as last-in-first-out and priority settings, ensuring the most relevant input source is always displayed.
Supports USB-C dual video mode, allowing one USB-C connection to transmit two independent video streams to two HDMI outputs.
Provides the ability to switch USB and video signals independently, offering greater flexibility in managing connected devices.
Compatible with mainstream audio DSPs and video bars, including brands such as Q-SYS, Shure, Biamp, Extron, Yealink, Logitech and more. For details, please refer to the USB compatibility list.
Compatible with Microsoft Teams Rooms(MTR), like Lenovo ThinkSmart Core Gen 1/2 devices.
Includes a balanced audio de-embedding port for connecting to audio equipment, ensuring high-quality audio output.
All ports support cable lock connections to ensure stable and secure connections for all devices during presentations.
Dual RJ-45 ports support Ethernet switching and VLAN settings, providing reliable network connectivity and enhanced security.
Supports firmware updates via the Web UI and offers multiple methods to restore factory settings, ensuring the device stays up-to-date and easy to troubleshoot.
USB-C ports support 100W Power Delivery, allowing for efficient charging of connected devices.
USB-C ports support 60W Power Delivery, allowing for efficient charging of connected devices.
